SECTION 2 — THE FIVE PIPELINE STEPS  (execute all five, in order)
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

STEP 1 · SPELLING & VALUE CORRECTION
  A. Verify botanical_name, genus, species, family spelling.
  B. Correct spelling errors in all free-text fields.
  C. Fix enum fields to match allowed values WORD-FOR-WORD.
  D. average_cost must be a float. id and quantity must be integers.
  E. grow_months and bloom_months must be exactly 12 characters.

STEP 2 · GAP FILLING
  A. Use botanical identity to fill every empty field with confidence.
  B. Only use values permitted by the schema in Section 1.
  C. Never change READ-ONLY fields.
  D. For chilling_hours: use the local chill hours context (Section 0).
  E. For company: follow the lookup order in Section 0.
  F. For average_cost: research current US retail price (Section 0).
  G. If less than 80% confident, leave empty — do not guess.

STEP 3 · SELF-VERIFICATION CHECK  (silent — fix before output)
  □ All enum values match allowed list word-for-word.
  □ grow_months and bloom_months are exactly 12 characters.
  □ average_cost is float. id and quantity are integers.
  □ All READ-ONLY fields unchanged from input.
  □ botanical_name, genus, species, family are correctly spelled in Latin.
  □ _missing_fields lists only genuinely empty fields.
  □ _enriched_fields lists every field touched.

STEP 4 · METADATA UPDATE
  _missing_fields  → Only fields still empty after your work.
  _enriched_fields → Every field you filled or corrected.

STEP 5 · FORMAT & OUTPUT
  • Output a single JSON Array  [ { ... } ]  — even for one plant.
  • Do NOT truncate any field values.
  • Do NOT add markdown or commentary inside the JSON block.
  • Every field from the schema must appear in every output object.
  • After the JSON block you may add a plain-text summary outside it.
